messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am having troubles to import my four way cross data to R using the read.cross function. Does anyone have examples of sample data for the three files so I can see what is different from mine ?
I got this error message when I try to import my data :

> data<-read.cross(format="mapqtl", mapfile = "ITmapfile.map",genfile = "ITgenofileb.loc",
+ phefile="phefile.csv", na.strings=c("--","*"),genotypes=NULL,dec=".")
Error in dimnames(x) <- dn :
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent
> traceback()
4: `rownames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = vapply(spl, "[", "", 1))
3: read.cross.mq.loc(locfile)
2: read.cross.mq <http://read.cross.mq>(dir = dir, locfile = genfile, mapfile = mapfile,
       quafile = phefile)
1: read.cross(format = "mapqtl", mapfile = "ITmapfile.map", genfile = "ITgenofileb.loc",
       phefile = "phefile.csv", na.strings = c("--", "*"), genotypes = NULL,
       dec = ".")
In my loc file, each marker has its information on the same line like recommanded but even then it does not work. So i think it is something to do with my files.

So I tried to find examples here http://www.rqtl.org/sampledata/ but there is none about the mapqtl format. Has anyone tried and achieved their data import ?

I would be grateful for your help so I can go further in my analysis.

Best regards,

Diana

messages.subject: Multiple libraries from vcftools
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I have genotype data (from ddRADseq of wild, F1, and F2 individuals) across three libraries that I want to concatenate for use in R/qtl. The cleanup (radtag processing, demultiplexing, removing PCR duplicates, alignment, etc.) was done by a collaborator, resulting in three separate .vcf files (one for each library). After my own quality filtering, I output each library to a 012 file (all through vcftools) and loaded those files into R to assemble data frames that would be usable in R/qtl. However, I'm not able to merge/join these data frames to analyze together due to different dimensions and loss of information (eg/ ‘marker 2’ in Lib01 is groupI 33579, whereas ‘marker 2’ in Lib02 is groupI 71336, and ‘marker 2’ in Lib 03 is groupI 149468).

This is my first stab at dealing with these data and I'm sure there are lots of people who have dealt with this before, I'm just having a hard time finding some direction for next steps. Do I need to go back to the original raw files and concatenate there, or are there steps I can take to do this with the processed data? Any and all advice or feedback would be greatly appreciated!

Cheers,

Sara

messages.body_plain:
Hello Sara:

There are some tools in GATK or Picard tools, try the following links for suggestion.

https://gatkforums.broadinstitute.org/gatk/discussion/53/combining-variants-from-different-files-into-one

There are MergeVcfs <https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/current/picard_vcf_MergeVcfs.php>, GatherVcfs <https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/current/picard_vcf_GatherVcfs.php> in Picard, CatVariants <https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/3.8-0/org_broadinstitute_gatk_tools_CatVariants.php>, CombineVariants <https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/3.8-0/org_broadinstitute_gatk_tools_walkers_variantutils_CombineVariants.php> in GATK.

These functions should consider if the samples are the same across vcfs, or the variants are the same across vcfs.

Maybe you can try CombineVariants <https://software.broadinstitute.org/gatk/documentation/tooldocs/3.8-0/org_broadinstitute_gatk_tools_walkers_variantutils_CombineVariants.php> first! But don’t forget to sort the vcfs before concatenate.

Don’t forget to consider the genotype quality which may depend on read depth in ddRAD library result.

Hope these will help…

Chun San

the tool for that very reason. Many examples in README and ./doc

Alternatively load the raw VCF data into R and write R-code to
re-organize it.

> This is my first stab at dealing with these data and I'm sure there are lots of people who have dealt with this before, I'm just having a hard time finding some direction for next steps. Do I need to go back to the original raw files and concatenate there, or are there steps I can take to do this with the processed data? Any and all advice or feedback would be greatly appreciated!

Dealing with VCF files to be my bread and butter at some point. It is
ugly.

Pj.
